newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sony sees more Singapore picture tube sale.
newsitem.headline: Sony sees more Singapore picture tube sale.

text.p: Sony Display Device (Singapore) Pte Ltd (SDS) projected sales from its Singapore picture tube plant to hit Singapore $600 million for the financial year ending March 1997, up from S$550 million in the previous year.
"It was S$550 million for year ending 1996, which is March. It will be S$600 million this year in March," Atsuo Inagaki told reporters at a briefing on Friday.
SDS, part of Sony Corp, announced a further investment of S$95 million in its Singapore plant to produce picture tubes for computer use.
That brings Sony's total investment in the plant, which will produce both picture tubes for television and display tubes for computers, to S$600 million.
The plant will start making display tubes for computers in April.
The initial output for computer use in 1997 will be 800,000 to 1.0 million tubes, rising to 1.5 million tubes annually, Inagaki said.
The entire plant will have a capacity of 7.5 million tubes, officials said. They said Sony makes a total of 10 million computer display tubes, seven million of them in Japan.
Inagaki declined to project sales from the Singapore plant for the 1997/98 financial year.
The bulk of Sony's computer picture tubes are for the group's own products' with two million pieces for customers like Apple Computer Inc and Hewlett Packard, officials said.
